lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.t: Ezekiel: overview
nodes.d: Ezekiel the priest, among the captives by the river Chebar in the fifth year of Jehoiachin's captivity, sees the glory of the LORD, announces the fall of Jerusalem, speaks against the nations, and sees promises of restoration and a new temple.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say where Ezekiel was and what the first chapter says happened to him?
ev: Say where and when Ezekiel received the word (1:1-3)
Describe the main movement of the book from judgment to restoration using the texts

nodes.t: Ezekiel's vision of the glory of the LORD
nodes.d: By the river Chebar Ezekiel sees a storm cloud with four living creatures, wheels full of eyes, a firmament, and above it a throne with a figure like a man in brightness; he falls on his face.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Ezekiel saw by the river Chebar and how he responded in Ezekiel 1:28?
ev: Describe the four living creatures and the wheels (1:5-21)
Describe the throne and what is on it (1:26-28)
Say how Ezekiel responds (1:28)

nodes.t: Ezekiel is sent to a rebellious house and eats a scroll
nodes.d: The Spirit raises Ezekiel, calls him "son of man", and sends him to a rebellious house with a scroll of lament, mourning and woe, which he eats, tasting sweet as honey; he is told Israel will not listen, and sits astonished among the exiles.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Ezekiel was commissioned and what he did with the scroll in Ezekiel 2-3?
ev: Describe what Ezekiel is sent to do (2:3-7)
Describe the scroll and what he does with it (2:9-3:3)
Say what the LORD says about Israel's hearing (3:7-9)

nodes.t: Ezekiel the watchman
nodes.d: After seven days the LORD makes Ezekiel a watchman for Israel, responsible to warn the wicked and the righteous; he is then told to shut himself in his house and made mute except when the LORD gives him words.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the duty of a watchman and what happens if he warns or does not warn in Ezekiel 3:17-21?
ev: Explain what the watchman is responsible for (3:17-21)
Describe what happens to Ezekiel's speech (3:26-27)

nodes.t: Signs of the siege of Jerusalem
nodes.d: Ezekiel draws Jerusalem on a tile with a siege against it, lies on his side for days bearing the iniquity of Israel and Judah, and eats rationed bread baked over dung as a sign of the famine and defiled bread to come.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the signs Ezekiel acts out in chapter 4 and what they stood for?
ev: Describe the tile and iron pan (4:1-3)
Describe the days he lies on each side (4:4-8)
Explain the bread and water (4:9-17)

nodes.t: The razor and the three parts
nodes.d: Ezekiel shaves his head and beard and divides the hair into thirds, burned, struck with a sword and scattered, as a sign of what the LORD will do in Jerusalem, set in the midst of the nations but worse than them in rejecting his statutes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the shaved hair divided in three stood for in Ezekiel 5:12?
ev: Describe how the hair is divided (5:1-2)
Explain what the three parts stand for (5:12)
Say why Jerusalem is judged (5:6-7, 11)

nodes.t: Prophecy to the mountains of Israel
nodes.d: Ezekiel prophesies against the mountains and high places of Israel: altars and idols will be broken, slain fall among their idols, and a remnant will remember the LORD among the nations and know he is the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Ezekiel 6 says will happen to the high places and what the remnant will remember?
ev: Say what is to happen to the altars and idols (6:3-6)
Describe the remnant (6:8-10)
Find the repeated phrase "ye shall know that I am the LORD"

nodes.t: The end has come upon the land
nodes.d: The LORD announces an end on the four corners of the land: wrath poured out according to ways, silver and gold unable to save, violence full in the land, and the temple given to strangers to defile.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what chapter 7 says silver and gold cannot do and what happens to the LORD's sanctuary?
ev: Describe the refrain "the end is come" (7:2-6)
Say what silver and gold cannot do (7:19)
Describe what happens to the beauty of the sanctuary (7:20-22)

nodes.t: The abominations in the temple
nodes.d: In the sixth year Ezekiel is carried in vision to Jerusalem and shown the image of jealousy, elders worshipping creeping things, women weeping for Tammuz, and men facing the sun in the temple; the LORD says he will not pity.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the abominations Ezekiel is shown in the temple in chapter 8 and what the LORD says he will do?
ev: List the four abominations Ezekiel is shown (8:5-16)
Say what the LORD says in response (8:17-18)

nodes.t: The man with the inkhorn and the slaughter
nodes.d: The LORD calls six men with weapons and a man in linen with an inkhorn who marks the foreheads of those who sigh over the city's abominations; those unmarked are struck beginning at the sanctuary, and Ezekiel pleads for the remnant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe who is marked and who is struck in Ezekiel 9?
ev: Describe the mark and who receives it (9:4)
Say where the slaughter begins (9:6)
Describe Ezekiel's plea and the answer (9:8-10)

nodes.t: The glory of the LORD leaves the temple threshold
nodes.d: Coals from between the cherubim are scattered over the city, Ezekiel sees the cherubim and wheels again, and the glory of the LORD moves off the threshold of the house and stands over the cherubim.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what the glory of the LORD does at the temple in Ezekiel 10:18-19?
ev: Describe the coals of fire (10:2-7)
Say how the cherubim are identified with those seen by the Chebar (10:15, 20)
Describe the movement of the glory (10:18-19)

nodes.t: The caldron, and the promise of a new heart
nodes.d: Ezekiel prophesies against leaders who treat Jerusalem as a caldron; the LORD promises to gather the scattered exiles, give them one heart, a new spirit and a heart of flesh in place of stone, and the glory leaves the city.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD promises to do for the scattered exiles in Ezekiel 11:17-20?
ev: Describe the leaders' saying and the LORD's answer (11:2-12)
Quote the promise in 11:17-20
Say where the glory goes (11:22-23)

nodes.t: Ezekiel packs for exile
nodes.d: Ezekiel carries his belongings through a hole in the wall as a sign of the prince's flight and exile to Babylon, eats his bread with trembling, and the LORD declares the proverbs that visions are far off will cease.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Ezekiel acts out exile in chapter 12 and what the LORD says about the saying that visions fail?
ev: Describe the sign Ezekiel acts out (12:3-7)
Say what the sign means for the prince (12:10-13)
Say what the LORD says about the proverb in 12:22-28

nodes.t: Against false prophets and prophetesses
nodes.d: The LORD is against prophets who follow their own spirit and say "peace" when there is none, like those daubing a wall with untempered mortar, and against women who prophesy from their own heart and hunt souls.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the picture of the wall daubed with untempered mortar in Ezekiel 13?
ev: Describe the whitewashed wall image (13:10-16)
Say what the women are charged with (13:17-23)

nodes.t: Idols in the heart
nodes.d: When elders come to enquire, the LORD says they have set idols in their hearts and calls Israel to repent; he will answer idolaters according to their idols.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what it means that the elders set up idols in their heart in Ezekiel 14:3-6?
ev: Say what the LORD says the elders have done (14:3)
Quote the call to repent (14:6)

nodes.t: Noah, Daniel and Job could only deliver themselves
nodes.d: The LORD says that even if Noah, Daniel and Job were in a land under four judgments, they would save only themselves; a remnant will survive Jerusalem's judgment so that the exiles will see it was not without cause.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say why the LORD names Noah, Daniel and Job in Ezekiel 14:14, 20 and what they could and could not do?
ev: Name the three men and what the LORD says of them (14:14, 20)
List the four judgments (14:21)
Say what the remnant will show the exiles (14:22-23)

nodes.t: The vine wood and the fire
nodes.d: The LORD compares Jerusalem's inhabitants to vine wood that is of no use for work, given to the fire as fuel, so that the land will be desolate.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the parable of the vine tree in Ezekiel 15?
ev: Explain the vine wood comparison (15:2-5)
Say what the LORD says he will do (15:6-8)

nodes.t: Jerusalem the foundling and unfaithful bride
nodes.d: The LORD describes finding Jerusalem as an unwanted newborn in the open field, raising her, covering her and making her beautiful, and then her trusting in her beauty, lavishing herself on idols and foreign nations and sacrificing her children.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what the LORD did for Jerusalem in Ezekiel 16:1-14 and how she responded?
ev: Retell what the LORD did for Jerusalem (16:4-14)
Describe how she responded (16:15-22)
Say what the LORD announces (16:35-43)

nodes.t: Sodom and Samaria as sisters and an everlasting covenant
nodes.d: Jerusalem is said to be worse than her sisters Samaria and Sodom, whose pride and neglect of the poor are named; the LORD will deal with her for breaking the oath but will remember his covenant and establish an everlasting covenant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Ezekiel 16:49 says Sodom's sin was and what the LORD promises in 16:60-62?
ev: Say what is said of Sodom's iniquity (16:49)
Say what the LORD says he will do despite her breaking the covenant (16:59-62)

nodes.t: The two eagles, the vine and the cedar twig
nodes.d: Ezekiel's riddle of two eagles and a vine is explained as the king of Babylon, a covenant broken by Zedekiah's turning to Egypt, and judgment; the LORD himself will plant a tender twig on the mountain of Israel to become a great cedar.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the riddle of the eagles and the vine and explain what it means in Ezekiel 17:11-21?
ev: Retell the riddle (17:3-10)
Explain its meaning (17:12-21)
Describe the LORD's planting (17:22-24)

nodes.t: The soul that sins shall die
nodes.d: The LORD rejects the proverb that fathers eat sour grapes and children's teeth are set on edge, saying each soul that sins dies, a person is judged by his own life, and the wicked who turn live; he has no pleasure in the death of the wicked.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Ezekiel 18 says about children bearing their fathers' guilt and about the wicked who turn?
ev: Say what proverb is rejected (18:2-3)
Describe the cases of the just father, wicked son and righteous grandson (18:5-18)

nodes.t: A lament for the princes of Israel
nodes.d: Ezekiel laments in two images: a lioness whose cubs are taken captive to Egypt and Babylon, and a vine in the water that is plucked up and left in the wilderness with its strong rod withered.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the two images in the lament of Ezekiel 19?
ev: Describe the lioness and her whelps (19:2-9)
Describe the vine (19:10-14)

nodes.t: Israel's rebellion from Egypt onward, and the LORD's gathering
nodes.d: When elders come to enquire, the LORD recounts Israel's rebellion from Egypt, in the wilderness and in the land, and his acting for his name's sake; he promises to gather them, plead with them face to face and bring them into the bond of the covenant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what reason the LORD gives for his actions in Ezekiel 20 and what he promises for the future?
ev: Retell what the LORD says of Egypt and the wilderness (20:5-26)
Say why he acted (20:9, 14, 22)
Describe his promise (20:33-44)

nodes.t: Fire in the forest of the south
nodes.d: Ezekiel is told to prophesy against the forest of the south: the LORD will kindle a fire that devours every green and dry tree and cannot be quenched; Ezekiel notes that people say he speaks in parables.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the fire in the forest of the south is like in Ezekiel 20:47-48?
ev: Describe the fire (20:47-48)
Say what the people say about Ezekiel (20:49)

nodes.t: The sword drawn and sharpened
nodes.d: The LORD draws his sword against the land and cuts off righteous and wicked; Ezekiel is told to sigh and prophesy of a sharpened sword, to mark two roads for the king of Babylon, and the crown of the profane prince is to be removed until he comes whose right it is.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the sword song of Ezekiel 21 and what the LORD says about the crown in 21:26-27?
ev: Describe the sword (21:3-5, 9-11)
Describe the two ways and the king of Babylon's divination (21:19-23)
Say what is promised in 21:25-27

nodes.t: The bloody city and the furnace
nodes.d: The LORD charges Jerusalem with bloodshed, idols and every kind of sin; the house of Israel is dross in a furnace, and he looked for someone to stand in the gap and found no one.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD looked for in Ezekiel 22:30 and what he found?
ev: List sins charged against the city (22:6-12)
Explain the furnace of 22:17-22
Say what the LORD sought and found (22:30)

nodes.t: Oholah and Oholibah
nodes.d: The LORD uses the story of two sisters, Samaria and Jerusalem, who pursued Assyria, Babylon and Egypt for their lovers, as a picture of Israel's and Judah's alliances and idolatry, and of the judgment on each.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who Oholah and Oholibah represent in Ezekiel 23 and what happens to them?
ev: Identify who the two sisters are (23:4)
Say what happens to Oholah (23:9-10)
Say what happens to Oholibah and why (23:22-35)

nodes.t: The boiling pot and the death of Ezekiel's wife
nodes.d: On the day Babylon besieges Jerusalem, the LORD gives a parable of a pot set on the fire; then Ezekiel's wife dies and he is told not to mourn publicly, as a sign that the people will lose the sanctuary and not mourn.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the sign of Ezekiel's wife's death in Ezekiel 24:15-24?
ev: Describe the pot parable (24:3-14)
Say what happens to Ezekiel's wife and what he is told (24:15-18)
Explain what the sign means (24:21-24)

nodes.t: Judgment on Ammon, Moab, Edom and Philistia
nodes.d: The LORD pronounces judgment on Ammon, Moab, Edom and the Philistines because they rejoiced over Judah's fall or took vengeance on her, so that they will know he is the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the nations judged in Ezekiel 25 and say why each is judged?
ev: Name the four nations and the reason for each judgment
Find the repeated phrase "they shall know that I am the LORD"

nodes.t: The fall of Tyre announced
nodes.d: Because Tyre rejoiced over Jerusalem's fall, the LORD says he will bring many nations against her, Nebuchadnezzar will besiege her, and she will become a bare rock for spreading nets; the isles and princes of the sea mourn.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say why Tyre is judged in Ezekiel 26 and what will become of her?
ev: Say why Tyre is judged (26:2)
Describe what Nebuchadnezzar does (26:7-12)
Describe the reaction of the princes of the sea (26:15-18)

nodes.t: A lament for Tyre the great ship
nodes.d: Ezekiel laments for Tyre as a magnificent merchant ship built by many nations and trading with them all, now wrecked in the heart of the sea, causing the seafarers and kings to mourn.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the picture of Tyre as a ship in Ezekiel 27 and what happens to it?
ev: Describe the ship and its builders (27:3-11)
List some of Tyre's trading partners (27:12-24)
Describe the shipwreck (27:26-36)

nodes.t: The prince and the king of Tyre
nodes.d: The prince of Tyre who says "I am a God" will die as a man at the hands of strangers; a lament over the king of Tyre describes him as full of wisdom and beauty, in Eden, the garden of God, on the holy mountain, until iniquity was found in him and he is cast down.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Ezekiel 28 charges the prince and the king of Tyre with and what happens to them?
ev: Say what the prince of Tyre claims and what will happen (28:2, 8-10)
Describe the king as pictured in 28:12-15
Say why he is cast down (28:16-18)

nodes.t: Zidon judged and Israel gathered to dwell safely
nodes.d: The LORD is against Zidon and will be glorified in her; afterward he will gather Israel from the peoples and they will dwell safely in the land, build houses and plant vineyards while he judges those around them who despised them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD promises Israel in Ezekiel 28:25-26 after judging the nations round about?
ev: Say what is said against Zidon (28:22-23)
Describe the promise to Israel (28:25-26)

nodes.t: Pharaoh the great dragon of the rivers
nodes.d: The LORD is against Pharaoh, the great dragon of the Nile, for saying the river is his and for being a broken reed to Israel; Egypt will be desolate forty years and then regathered as a lowly kingdom, and Nebuchadnezzar is given Egypt as wages for the labour against Tyre.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how the LORD speaks of Pharaoh in Ezekiel 29 and what Egypt is promised after forty years?
ev: Describe Pharaoh's fault and the picture used (29:3-9)
Say what happens after forty years (29:13-16)
Say what Nebuchadnezzar is given and why (29:17-20)

nodes.t: The day of the LORD against Egypt
nodes.d: A day of the LORD is near for Egypt and her allies; Nebuchadnezzar's sword brings destruction to its cities, and the LORD breaks Pharaoh's arms while strengthening Babylon's.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD says he will do to the arms of Pharaoh and of the king of Babylon in Ezekiel 30?
ev: Say who falls with Egypt (30:4-5)
Describe what happens to Pharaoh's arms (30:21-25)

nodes.t: Pharaoh compared to the great cedar
nodes.d: The LORD compares Pharaoh to the Assyrian, a mighty cedar in Lebanon whose height made it proud and which was cut down by foreigners, as a warning to those who exalt themselves.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the picture of the cedar and why it was cut down in Ezekiel 31?
ev: Describe the cedar and its greatness (31:3-9)
Say why it was brought down (31:10-14)

nodes.t: Lament for Pharaoh and the nations in the pit
nodes.d: Ezekiel laments over Pharaoh as a sea monster caught in the LORD's net; Egypt and its multitude are described going down to the pit, where Asshur, Elam, Meshech, Tubal, Edom and other nations already lie.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the lament over Pharaoh in Ezekiel 32 and name some nations said to lie in the pit?
ev: Describe Pharaoh as a creature in the sea and his fate (32:2-8)
Say which nations are already in the pit (32:22-30)

nodes.t: The watchman and "Why will ye die?"
nodes.d: The LORD repeats the watchman charge to Ezekiel and tells him to say he has no pleasure in the death of the wicked but that they turn and live; he insists each person is judged according to his ways.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD says in Ezekiel 33:11 and explain the duty of the watchman?
ev: Describe the watchman parable (33:2-6)
Quote 33:11
Explain what is said of the righteous who turn to sin and the wicked who turn from it (33:12-19)

nodes.t: News of the fall of Jerusalem
nodes.d: An escapee tells Ezekiel in the twelfth year of captivity that the city has been struck down, and Ezekiel's mouth is opened; the LORD rebukes those in the ruined land who claim it, and the exiles who hear Ezekiel as a pleasant song without doing his words.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what Ezekiel was told in 33:21 and how the LORD says the people listen to him in 33:30-32?
ev: Retell what happens when the escapee arrives (33:21-22)
Say what those in the wastes say and the LORD's reply (33:24-29)
Describe how the people listen to Ezekiel (33:30-33)

nodes.t: The shepherds of Israel and the LORD the shepherd
nodes.d: The LORD condemns shepherds who feed themselves and scatter his flock, promises to seek and gather his sheep himself, to judge between the fat and lean, and to set one shepherd, his servant David, over them with a covenant of peace.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how the LORD will shepherd his flock and who he sets over it in Ezekiel 34:11-24?
ev: Describe the shepherds' failure (34:2-6)
Say what the LORD promises to do himself (34:11-16)
Describe the one shepherd and the covenant of peace (34:23-25)

nodes.t: Against Mount Seir
nodes.d: The LORD is against Mount Seir (Edom) for perpetual hatred and for claiming the lands of Israel and Judah, and will make it desolate.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say why the LORD speaks against Mount Seir in Ezekiel 35?
ev: Say why Mount Seir is judged (35:5, 10-12)
Say what the LORD says he will do (35:14-15)

nodes.t: The mountains of Israel will bear fruit again
nodes.d: The LORD speaks to the mountains of Israel, which the nations have mocked, promising that his people will return, cities be rebuilt, the land be fruitful, and the land no longer devour men or bear the nations' reproach.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD promises to the mountains of Israel in Ezekiel 36:8-12?
ev: Say what the nations said and the LORD's answer (36:2-7)
Describe the promise to the mountains (36:8-12)

nodes.t: I will sprinkle clean water and give a new heart and spirit
nodes.d: The LORD says he will act for his holy name, not Israel's sake: he will gather them, sprinkle clean water on them, give a new heart and put his Spirit within them so they keep his statutes, and make the land like Eden.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what the LORD promises to do in Ezekiel 36:24-28?
ev: Say why the LORD acts (36:21-23)
List what he promises in 36:24-28
Describe the land after cleansing (36:33-36)

nodes.t: The valley of dry bones
nodes.d: The Spirit sets Ezekiel in a valley of very dry bones and asks if they can live; as Ezekiel prophesies, bones, sinews, flesh and breath come into them as an exceeding great army, which the LORD says is the whole house of Israel he will raise from their graves.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the vision of the valley of dry bones and say what the bones stand for in Ezekiel 37:11-14?
ev: Retell what Ezekiel sees and is told to do (37:1-10)
Say what the bones represent (37:11)
Say what the LORD promises (37:12-14)

nodes.t: Two sticks made one and a covenant of peace
nodes.d: Ezekiel joins two sticks marked for Judah and for Joseph to show the LORD will make them one nation under one king, David his servant, with a covenant of peace, an everlasting covenant, and his sanctuary among them for evermore.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the sign of the two sticks and what covenant the LORD promises in Ezekiel 37:15-28?
ev: Describe the sign with the two sticks (37:16-17)
Say who rules and what covenant is made (37:22-26)
Say what the LORD places among them (37:26-28)

nodes.t: Gog of Magog comes against Israel
nodes.d: The LORD sets himself against Gog, prince of Meshech and Tubal, who with many allies will come from the north in the latter years against Israel dwelling safely, and the LORD brings him with earthquake, sword, pestilence and fire so that nations know he is the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe who Gog is and what happens when he comes against Israel in Ezekiel 38?
ev: Describe Gog and his allies (38:2-6)
Say when and against whom he comes (38:8, 11-12, 16)
Describe how the LORD acts (38:19-23)

nodes.t: Gog defeated and Israel restored
nodes.d: Gog and his army fall on the mountains of Israel, weapons are burned for seven years and the dead buried over seven months, birds and beasts feast, and the LORD says he will bring back the captivity of Jacob and pour out his Spirit on Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what happens to Gog's army in Ezekiel 39 and what the LORD promises Israel at the end?
ev: Describe the end of Gog's army (39:2-6)
Describe the burning of weapons and burial (39:9-16)
Say what the LORD promises Israel (39:25-29)

nodes.t: The vision of the temple: the man with the measuring reed
nodes.d: In the twenty-fifth year of the exile Ezekiel is taken in visions of God to a high mountain in Israel and led by a man with a line and measuring reed through the gates and courts of a new temple complex, with tables for sacrifices and chambers for priests.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how the vision of the temple begins in Ezekiel 40:1-5 and what Ezekiel is told to do?
ev: Describe the man and what he tells Ezekiel to do (40:3-4)
Describe the gates and courts measured (40:5-47)

nodes.t: The temple house, its chambers and the walled area
nodes.d: The man measures the temple house with its side chambers, panelling carved with cherubim and palm trees, the priests' holy chambers, and the outer wall around the whole to separate the holy from the common.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the carvings in the temple in Ezekiel 41 were and what the wall around it was for in 42:20?
ev: Describe the carvings on the walls and doors (41:18-20, 25)
Say what the priests' chambers are for (42:13-14)
Say what the surrounding wall is for (42:20)

nodes.t: The glory of the LORD returns to the temple
nodes.d: The glory of the LORD comes into the house by the east gate and fills it; he says it is the place of his throne where he will dwell among Israel for ever if they put away their idolatry, and the altar and its consecration are described.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how the glory of the LORD enters the temple in Ezekiel 43:1-5 and what the LORD says in 43:7?
ev: Describe how the glory comes (43:2-5)
Say what the LORD says about his dwelling (43:7-9)
Describe the altar and its consecration (43:13-27)

nodes.t: The shut east gate and the ministers of the sanctuary
nodes.d: The east gate is shut for the prince alone; the LORD rebukes Israel for admitting uncircumcised strangers, and distinguishes the Levites who strayed from the sons of Zadok who kept charge of the sanctuary and may minister, with rules for their dress and conduct.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who the LORD says may minister in his sanctuary in Ezekiel 44 and who may not?
ev: Describe the shut gate (44:1-3)
Say who may and may not minister (44:9-16)
Say what the priests are to teach (44:23-24)

nodes.t: The holy portion, the prince and just measures
nodes.d: The land is divided with a holy portion for the sanctuary, priests, Levites, city and prince; princes are told to end violence, use just weights, and provide offerings at the feasts.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the princes of Israel are told to do in Ezekiel 45:9-10?
ev: Say who receives the portions (45:1-8)
Quote the command to the princes (45:9-10)
Say what the prince provides at the feasts (45:17-25)

nodes.t: Worship of the prince and people and the temple kitchens
nodes.d: The prince and people worship at the east gate on sabbaths and new moons with prescribed offerings; the prince may not take inheritances from the people, and kitchens for priests and for the people's sacrifices are shown.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the prince is forbidden to do with the people's inheritance in Ezekiel 46:18?
ev: Describe when the east gate is open (46:1-3)
Say what the prince may not do (46:18)
Describe the kitchens (46:19-24)

nodes.t: The river flowing from the temple
nodes.d: Water flows from under the threshold of the temple and grows from ankle-deep to a river that cannot be crossed, flows east into the Dead Sea healing its waters, and trees on its banks bear fruit every month with leaves for healing.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the river from the temple in Ezekiel 47:1-12 and what it does?
ev: Describe the river and its depths (47:1-5)
Say what happens where the river goes (47:8-9)
Describe the trees (47:12)

nodes.t: The borders of the land and the strangers' share
nodes.d: The LORD gives the borders of the land to be divided among the twelve tribes by lot, with strangers who live among them also receiving inheritance in the tribe where they live.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Ezekiel 47:22-23 says about foreigners living among Israel?
ev: Name the sea and river borders (47:15-20)
Say what is said of strangers (47:22-23)

nodes.t: The tribal portions and the city called The LORD is there
nodes.d: The land is divided into parallel portions for the twelve tribes with a central holy district for priests, Levites, city and prince; the city has twelve gates named for the tribes and its name from that day is The LORD is there.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the city is called at the end of Ezekiel 48 and what its gates are named for?
ev: Describe the arrangement of tribal portions (48:1-7, 23-29)
Name the city's gates (48:31-34)
Quote the city's new name (48:35)

nodes.t: Jeremiah: overview
nodes.d: Jeremiah son of Hilkiah, a priest of Anathoth, receives the word of the LORD from the thirteenth year of Josiah to the exile after Zedekiah's eleventh year, warning Judah of judgment from the north and promising restoration and a new covenant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who Jeremiah was and during whose reigns the word of the LORD came to him according to Jeremiah 1:1-3?
ev: Name the kings during whose reigns the word came (Jeremiah 1:1-3)
Explain that the book is not arranged only in the order of the events it describes, using examples from its dates

nodes.t: Everlasting love: Israel gathered and Rachel comforted
nodes.d: The LORD loves Israel with an everlasting love and will gather them from the north, redeem them and turn mourning to joy; Rachel weeps for her children but the LORD promises they will return, and the new thing and the sour grape saying are addressed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD promises in Jeremiah 31:3 and 31:15-17?
ev: Quote Jeremiah 31:3
Describe Rachel's weeping and the promise (31:15-17)
Explain the saying about the sour grape that will no longer be used (31:29-30)

nodes.t: The new covenant
nodes.d: The LORD promises a new covenant with Israel and Judah, unlike the one broken after the exodus: he will write his law on their hearts, they will all know him, and he will forgive their iniquity and remember their sin no more.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what is new about the covenant promised in Jeremiah 31:31-34?
ev: Say whom the covenant is made with and what it is unlike (31:31-32)
Describe what the LORD does in 31:33
Quote the promise of forgiveness in 31:34

nodes.t: The throne in heaven
nodes.d: John is called up through an open door and sees a throne with one sitting on it, a rainbow, twenty-four elders in white with crowns, four living creatures crying holy, holy, holy, and all worship God as Creator.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the throne room scene and what the worshippers say?
ev: Describe what surrounds the throne
Say what the four beasts and the elders say and do
Say why God is worthy according to 4:11
